title: Writing the Last Scene First
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece borrows John Grisham's advice to write the last scene first and applies it to leadership strategy. The author argues that leaders should write the last chapter before designing a strategy, so they know exactly where it must lead. A vivid end state goes beyond goals and outcomes to include impact, reputation, new constituents and effects on processes, workflows and resources. Listing outcomes comes first, then the differences others will see, then the brand or reputation that results. Working backward from this defined endpoint sharpens the strategy and makes it easier to align actions and investments. The closing claim is that a highly defined end state takes the mystery out of crafting a strategy.
points: Defining the last chapter first lets leaders craft a more complete and accurate strategy.
A rich end state includes goals, impact, reputation, new constituents and effects on workflows and resources.
Working backward from a specific end state makes it easier to align actions and initiatives.
Spelling out the full end state reveals the investments and steps the strategy must contain.
quotes: Suspense writer John Grisham has this advice for mystery novelists: Don’t write the first scene until you’ve written the last. When a writer knows exactly how matters are going to wrap up, they can compose a more compelling story to get there.
This advice also applies perfectly to leaders who are crafting a strategy. Strategies are more on target when leaders write the last chapter first.

Beyond goals and outcomes, a vivid end game includes a description of impact, reputation, offshoot opportunities, and new constituents, among other features. By writing a thorough synopsis of the endpoint, leaders are able to craft a more complete and accurate strategy to arrive there.

Of course, the future state is comprised of attainable goals, both broad and narrow. Listing the many outcomes and goals that describe the ideal end state is a good first step. Next, a description of the primary impact of achieving the goals and the many differences others will see in the end state adds much-needed texture.

By working backward from a highly defined last chapter, the strategy for going forward to achieve it comes into sharper focus. It becomes easier to align actions and initiatives with the desired outcomes. Figuring out the many investments and steps required to achieve the end state in its entirety makes the strategy more robust and complete.

Sound strategy starts with having a highly defined end state, full of goals and other aspirational features. By writing the last chapter first, good leaders take the mystery out of crafting a great strategy. John Grisham would be pleased.
